function.name: ProductSearch_execute
function.description: Performs a search for products in the database based on specified criteria, such as keywords and filters, and returns a list of matching products. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

keywords.description: The search terms used to find products, separated by spaces.

category.description: The category to filter the search results. If no category is specified, all categories will be included in the search.

price_range.description: A price range to narrow down the search results, specified as a string in the format 'min-max' where min and max are prices in USD.

sort_order.description: The order in which the search results are sorted. Choose 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending order.

in_stock.description: A flag to filter search results to only include products that are in stock. Set to true to include only in-stock items.

message.content:
Cream is a classic, versatile shade that can work well in many contexts, but whether it’s the right choice for you depends on a few factors. Here’s a quick guide to help you decide: | Factor | How Cream Works | Tips | |--------|-----------------|------| | **Skin tone** | • **Cool undertones**: Cream can look a bit washed out; pair it with cool neutrals (gray, navy, charcoal) or add a pop of color (emerald, cobalt).
• **Warm undertones**: Cream complements your natural warmth beautifully. Pair it with earthy tones (olive, terracotta, mustard) or keep it monochromatic for a subtle look.
• **Neutral undertones**: Cream is a safe bet; you can mix it with both cool and warm hues. | • Test by holding a cream fabric against your face in natural light.
• If it looks too pale, consider a slightly deeper beige or taupe. | | **Occasion** | • **Casual**: Cream chinos, a cream tee, or a cream cardigan can look relaxed yet polished.
• **Business/Professional**: Cream dress shirts or blazers pair nicely with darker suits (navy, charcoal).
• **Formal**: Cream tuxedo jackets or suits are elegant, especially in spring/summer.
• **Outdoor/Beach**: Cream linen or cotton is breathable and keeps you cool. | • For formal events, add a contrasting tie or pocket square to avoid looking too “washed out.” | | **Season** | • **Spring/Summer**: Cream is a great light, airy choice.
• **Fall/Winter**: Cream can feel too bright; pair it with deeper colors or layer with a dark coat. | • In cooler months, layer cream tops under wool coats or sweaters for contrast. | | **Color Coordination** | • Cream pairs well with: navy, charcoal, burgundy, forest green, mustard, blush pink, and even black.
• Avoid pairing cream with pure white or very pale pastels unless you’re aiming for a monochrome look. | • Use accessories (scarves, belts, shoes) in complementary colors to anchor the outfit. | | **Fabric & Texture** | • Light fabrics (cotton, linen, silk) keep the look airy.
• Heavier fabrics (wool, tweed) add depth and are great for cooler weather. | • A cream knit sweater over a crisp shirt can create a layered, stylish look. | ### Quick Decision Checklist 1. **What’s the event?** - Casual → Cream chinos + tee or cardigan. - Business → Cream shirt or blazer with darker suit. - Formal → Cream tuxedo or suit. 2. **What’s your skin tone?** - Cool → Add a cool accent color. - Warm → Cream works naturally. 3. **What season?** - Spring/Summer → Cream is perfect. - Fall/Winter → Layer or pair with darker hues. 4. **Do you have a favorite color to pair with?** - If you love navy or charcoal, cream is a great complement. ### Bottom Line - **Yes, wear cream-colored clothes** if you’re aiming for a fresh, neutral look that’s versatile across many occasions, especially if you have warm undertones or are dressing for spring/summer. - **Consider pairing it with a contrasting color** (navy, charcoal, burgundy) to add depth and avoid a washed‑out appearance. - **If you’re unsure**, try a cream top or accessory first and see how it feels with your skin tone and the rest of your wardrobe. Feel free to let me know more about your style preferences, skin tone, or upcoming events, and I can give you more tailored suggestions!
